title: Bigger Is Not Better: Effectiveness | Principles of Management Ep 28
description:
Chai Corner began as one stall, with Ravi doing everything alone. Now it has five outlets and a head office. But is it actually doing well? Kabir says sales are up, Asha asks if the staff are happy, and Meena asks about the customers. In this series finale we use Ravi's chai chain to learn how to judge a whole organization.

You will learn what organizational effectiveness means (how well an organization achieves its goals, a report card for the whole organization, not one number), and the difference between effective (doing the right things) and efficient (doing things right) on a simple two by two grid. Then we watch Ravi run all four ways to judge effectiveness on his report card: the goal approach, the resource approach, the internal process approach and the stakeholder approach. We look back at Ravi's whole journey from one stall to five outlets, and see five signs managers keep score with at work today: profit, productivity, customer satisfaction, employee satisfaction and adaptability, from a bakery and a factory to a hotel and a shop that moves online. We also look at the human side: the scorecard trap that British economist Charles Goodhart pointed to in 1975, and why different groups want different things.

This is Episode 28, the final episode of our Principles of Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
